packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-06 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context proposed an identification of this leaf or a reading of it.
My context does contain general notes that the caller runs a manuscript-fragment
project, but no work, author or shelfmark for this packet. I opened only PROMPT.md
and image-001..007 of this packet (plus the reader brief). No web, no search, no
packet.json. I do not attempt to name the work or author.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: overview of one face of a narrow vertical strip (roughly 55-60 mm wide
  by about 150 mm tall by the scale), upright orientation, heavily torn at top,
  left edge and lower left, with holes and modern tissue repairs (grey fibrous
  patches). Brown ink.
- One narrow text block survives, occupying the left ~2/3 of the strip. Its left
  edge is torn away: every line has lost its beginning. The right edge of the
  written lines looks like a real line end (ragged right, then blank parchment),
  so the strip seems to preserve the right-hand part of a column plus an outer or
  intercolumnar margin. That is an interpretation.
- A vertical ruling/fold line runs down the right third. To the right of it, at the
  extreme right edge, are short dark strokes arranged vertically (image-002 right
  edge, about a third and two thirds down). They look like the cut-off beginnings
  of lines of another column, or offset; I cannot read them.
- Script: small, rapid, extremely abbreviated cursive bookhand; about 19 lines in
  the upper block.
- No running title, no rubric, no coloured initial, no underlining visible.
- One struck-through word (image-002 line 13 / image-003 line 2): a horizontal
  line through the first word of the line.
- After the upper block there is a wavy horizontal pen stroke across the column
  (image-003, below line 10), then a line beginning with a word in larger, darker
  letters (image-003 line 11). Tentative interpretation: end of one section and
  start of a new one (heading or new question/paragraph). Below that the hand
  looks smaller/more compressed and partly a darker ink, and the lines run further
  right, into the margin, slanting; this may be an addition or note in a second
  hand rather than the continuation of the main column. Uncertain.
- image-005 (overview), image-006, image-007 (tiles): the other face. I see no
  writing on it at all: stained blank parchment, a line of faint grey specks down
  the middle (possibly show-through or dirt along a fold), repairs, and a modern
  pencil mark on the paper tab at the top ("x/0"?? - on the modern support, not on
  the leaf). Nothing to transcribe from this face.

SPANS SELECTED
A. image-002, lines 5-14: best preserved connected stretch of the upper block.
B. image-003, lines 1-10: continuation to the wavy divider (lines 1-3 repeat
   image-002 lines 12-14: overlap, not new text).
C. image-003 lines 11-18 and image-004 lines 1-7: the text below the divider.
Unread: image-002 lines 1-4 (only letter-tops and scraps on a detached, crumpled
piece), and the right-edge marginal strokes.

The script is so abbreviated and the line beginnings so consistently lost that most
of what follows is tentative. I give what the letter shapes seem to be; expansions
in parentheses are proposals, not readings.

TRANSCRIPTION

Span A - image-002 (line numbers from top of image; beginnings of all lines torn off)
image-002 l.1  [scraps only: tops of letters] ... a(?)lig(?)ue(?) [illegible]
image-002 l.2  [illegible] ... due(?) [hole]
image-002 l.3  [illegible] ... ista(?) / illa(?)
image-002 l.4  [..]allic(?)[..] [repair] ... d(icu)nt(?)
image-002 l.5  ] e(st) ead(em) i(n)[..] q(uod) a(liqu)is(?) q(uod) illa
image-002 l.6  ] vnig(e)n(i)ti(?) accip(itu)r(?) e(st)(?) h(oc)(?)
image-002 l.7  ] ill(a) filia(ti)o(?) sic(?) d(e)mo(n)st(ra)t(ur)(?)   [or: de(ter)mi(n)at(ur)?]
image-002 l.8  ] vnic(a)(?) e(st) duob(us) q(ui)cu(m)q(ue)(?)
image-002 l.9  ] dic(itu)r q(uia) e(ss)et(?) disti(n)cta(?) s(ed) ead(em)
image-002 l.10 ]a filia(ti)o(?) vnica i(n) ea(?) int(e)ll(ect)us(?)
image-002 l.11 ] a duob(us) ex dist(in)ct(is)(?) e(ss)e(?) s(ed)
image-002 l.12 ]s(?) q(uod) d(e)mo(n)st(ra)t(i)o(?) i(n)tellex(it)(?)
image-002 l.13 ] [one word struck through with a horizontal line, apparently the same
               word as "d(e)mo(n)st(ra)..." of l.12, followed by two short strokes]
               Similit(er) qui
image-002 l.14 ] p(ro)ced(er)e(?) p(ro)p(ter)(?) ead(em) p(ri)uat(?)
image-002 l.15 [cut by crop; see image-003 l.4]

The words I am least unsure of in span A: "est eadem", "illa", "duobus", "unica",
"eadem", "a duobus", "Similiter qui". The repeated word I render "filia(ti)o" is
written "fill-" with superscript; it could equally be "fill9" = fili(us), which is
how I read it in image-003 l.4. The word I render "d(e)mo(n)st(ra)-" (lines 7, 12,
13) is a guess from "d", minims, "st", suspension; "determinat-" or "denominat-"
are also possible.

Span B - image-003
image-003 l.1  = image-002 l.12 (overlap)
image-003 l.2  = image-002 l.13 (overlap; the struck-through word is clear here as a
               deletion)
image-003 l.3  = image-002 l.14 (overlap): ] p(ro)ced(er)e(?) [..] p(ro)p(ter)(?) ead(em) p(ri)uat(?)
image-003 l.4  ] q(uod)(?) p(ro)cedit fili(us) simpl(icite)r   [a long stroke runs on
               to the right after "simpl'"]
image-003 l.5  ]u(n)t(?) dic(itu)r q(uod)(?) s(un)t de ead(em) diui[..]tez(?)   [last word
               "d'uolez"/"diuolez"-like; I cannot resolve it]
image-003 l.6  ] s(ed)(?) ex[hole]nif(est)is(?) [..]ab(us)(?) q(uas)i diuidi(?)   [or c(on)sid(er)ati?]
image-003 l.7  ] q(uod)(?) [hole]s(?)te p(ro)(?) ex eis s(ed) loc(us)(?)
image-003 l.8  ] [..]u(a)le(?) q(ui)a(?) [..] ead(em)(?) c(on)sid(er)at(ur)(?)
image-003 l.9  ] [..] q(uod)(?) [..]c(?) c(ausa)(?) d(i)c(tu)m sit
image-003 l.10 [wavy horizontal pen stroke across the column - a divider, not text]

Span C - below the divider
image-003 l.11 ] [larger, darker letters] V(?)[.]lln / "ill(u)m"(?) [faded word] [..]a(?) amet(?)/a(n)i(m)e(?)
               [ends in a long ascending flourish to the right]
               The enlarged word has a tall first letter, then minims with an
               abbreviation stroke above; "Vtrum" is possible but I cannot confirm
               it from the shapes.
image-003 l.12 ] [faded] ... a(?)d(?)... [repair]
image-003 l.13 ] [repair] ... hic(?) / d(i)c(i)t(?)
image-003 l.14 ] s(ed)(?) q(uia)(?) [faded] ... [..]mit(?)
image-003 l.15 ] [..] thom[..](?) vnig(e)n(i)ti(?) / "vng(?)ecto(rum)" [..] yssi(?) sec(?)
               [reading of every word doubtful; begins with a dash-like stroke]
image-003 l.16 ] [repair] ... c(a)p(itul)i(?) (et)(?) [..]alla(?)   [written higher on the right,
               darker ink, possibly a separate short note]
image-003 l.17 ] v(er)e(?) po(ss)it(?) [repair] [..]q(ue)(?) [..] ut dixit(?)   [followed by a
               long oblique stroke]
image-003 l.18 [cut by crop; see image-004 l.4]

image-004 (lower tile; lines 1-3 overlap image-003 lines 15-17)
image-004 l.1  = image-003 l.15 (overlap)
image-004 l.2  = image-003 l.16 (overlap)
image-004 l.3  = image-003 l.17 (overlap): ] [..]mosti(?)/"v(er)e possi(t)"(?) ... ut dixit(?)
image-004 l.4  ] iu(?)[..] [hole] noss(?)e(?)m(us)(?) [..]a(?) sci(?)[..]   [or "p(ro)ssean ... fa(cta)"?]
image-004 l.5  ] occ(?)ad(?)[hole] [..]d(?)cc(?)el(?) s(ecundu)m(?) [..]
image-004 l.6  ] [..] [..] ex(?)[..] t(er)cii(?)/"t(er)re" [..] [faint, lighter ink:] ma4(?)
image-004 l.7  [no further text; below is blank, torn parchment]

Other face (image-005, -006, -007): no text visible.

LIMITATIONS
- Every line lacks its beginning (left edge torn); line ends appear complete. Width
  lost on the left is unknown, so no line gives a complete sense unit.
- Top four lines are on a crumpled, partly detached scrap and are essentially
  unreadable from these images.
- The hand is highly abbreviated and cursive; at native resolution the ink is
  blurred and many abbreviation marks cannot be told apart. The individual words
  marked (?) should not be used as match evidence on their own. The safest
  material for a later check is the sequence: "... est eadem ... illa / ... / ...
  unica(?) est duobus ... / ... sed eadem / ... unica ... / a duobus ... / ... /
  [deleted word] Similiter qui / ... procedere(?) ... eadem ... / ... procedit
  fili(us) simpl(icite)r / ... dicitur ... sunt de eadem ... / ... dictum sit",
  followed by a pen divider and a new start in larger letters.
- Whether the text below the divider belongs to the same hand and text is not
  certain.
- The strokes at the far right edge are probably the edge of neighbouring writing
  but are not readable.
- Suggested additional views: a raking-light or UV/IR image of this face
  (especially the top scrap and the lines below the divider), and any adjoining
  strip that would supply the lost left half of the column.
